nanjing.blurb: Ming capital since 1368, Nanjing was ringed by a Capital City wall more than 30 km long. In 1400 the Jianwen Emperor ruled here while at war with his uncle Zhu Di, who would seize the city in 1402.

image.file: File:Nanjing-Zhonghua-Gate-3071.jpg
image.caption: The Zhonghua Gate complex on the southern side of the Nanjing city wall, photographed in 2008.

vijayanagara.blurb: On the banks of the Tungabhadra River, Vijayanagara was capital of an empire that Harihara II (r. 1377–1404) had consolidated beyond the Krishna River, bringing South India under its control.

image.file: File:Ruins of Vijianuggur, the market in front of Virupaksha temple also called Hampi bazaar, Hampi, Vijayanagara, 1868 photo.jpg
image.caption: The ruined bazaar street in front of the Virupaksha temple at Hampi, photographed by Edmund David Lyon in 1868.

cairo.blurb: Capital of the Mamluk Sultanate, now ruled by the Burji Mamluks, Cairo was still reeling from repeated plague and political instability since 1348. The era had nonetheless produced the Madrasa-Mosque of Sultan Hasan, the largest Mamluk-era religious monument.

image.file: File:Mosque of Sultan Hasan, Cairo.jpg
image.caption: The Madrasa-Mosque of Sultan Hasan, the largest Mamluk-era religious monument in Cairo, photographed in 2012.

paris.blurb: Paris lay inside the new wall Charles V had built between 1356 and 1383, guarded by his Bastille fortress. But plague kept returning and the Hundred Years' War dragged on; the English would take the city in 1420.

image.file: File:Les Très Riches Heures du duc de Berry octobre.jpg
image.caption: October page of the Très Riches Heures du duc de Berry, painted between 1412 and 1416, with the Louvre fortress behind the Seine.

hangzhou.blurb: The former Southern Song capital, at the southern end of the Grand Canal, was slowly regaining its prosperity under the Ming. Its West Lake, neglected under the Mongols and partly turned into farmland, still awaited restoration.

image.file: File:Su Causeway, West Lake.jpg
image.caption: The Su Causeway across West Lake, built from dredged silt in 1089, photographed in 2011.

beijing.blurb: Ming capital since 1421, Beijing centred on the Forbidden City, built 1406–1420. Imperial granaries near the Grand Canal's terminus fed its people, who had switched to coal once the surrounding forests were cut down.

image.file: File:Verbotene-Stadt1500.jpg
image.caption: Detail of the Beijing Palace City Scroll, painted in the mid-Ming dynasty (c. 15th century), showing the Forbidden City.

vijayanagara.blurb: By 1500 Vijayanagara was probably India's richest city, drawing traders from Persia and Portugal. Power lay with the regent Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, who defended the empire against the Gajapati king and the Bahmani Sultan.

image.file: File:Hampi Vitthala Temple 3465.jpg
image.caption: The Vitthala temple complex in the ruins of Vijayanagara at Hampi, photographed in 2019.

cairo.blurb: Sultan Qaytbay (r. 1468–1496) had built or restored numerous monuments in Cairo, but after him the crisis of Mamluk power deepened, and a new sea route around Africa soon let spice traders bypass the city.

image.file: File:Qaytbay complex.jpg
image.caption: Sultan Qaytbay's mosque and mausoleum complex in Cairo's Northern Cemetery, photographed in 2012.

hangzhou.blurb: Hangzhou's harbour was slowly silting up, and the city acted as a feeder to the larger Suzhou market along the Grand Canal. In 1508 governor Yang Mengying would dredge West Lake, repairing its causeways and adding a new one.

image.file: File:Ming Dynasty Hangzhou City Map.jpg
image.caption: Map of Hangzhou's prefectural seat under the Ming dynasty, originally made in 1547.

tabriz.blurb: Capital of the Aq Qoyunlu since 1469, Tabriz kept monuments of its earlier Qara Qoyunlu rulers, including the Blue Mosque. In 1501 Ismail I would enter the city and proclaim it capital of his new Safavid state.

image.file: File:-Blue Mosque of TABRIZ, 1465.- MET DP202986.jpg
image.caption: The Blue Mosque of Tabriz, built in 1465, photographed in the mid-19th century.

1600.note: Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory at the Battle of Sekigahara in October 1600 made him Japan's paramount warlord; in 1603 he founded the Tokugawa shogunate at Edo.

beijing.blurb: Beijing now had an Outer City wall, added in 1553 after a Mongol raid. In 1601 the Jesuit Matteo Ricci became an adviser to the Wanli Emperor and the first Westerner admitted to the Forbidden City.

image.file: File:Departure Herald-Ming Dynasty.jpg
image.caption: Departure Herald, a Ming handscroll from the Jiajing reign (1522–1566) showing the emperor's procession leaving Beijing for the imperial tombs.

istanbul.blurb: In Eminönü, Constantinople's busiest commercial quarter, Safiye Sultan, mother of Mehmed III, began a vast mosque in 1597. The Janissaries resented its cost, and work stopped in 1603, leaving it unfinished for decades.

image.file: File:Ca. 1600 bird's eye view map of Constantinople.jpg
image.caption: Bird's-eye view map of Constantinople made around 1600.

agra.blurb: In 1599 Akbar moved the Mughal capital back to Agra from Lahore, returning to the red sandstone fort he had rebuilt in 1565–1573. The English traveller Ralph Fitch had called Agra much greater than London.

image.file: File:Bau der Festung von Agra (rechte Hälfte).jpg
image.caption: Building the fort at Agra in 1565, an illustration from the Akbarnama painted around 1590 (Victoria and Albert Museum).

osaka.blurb: Toyotomi Hideyoshi completed Osaka Castle, with its gold-leafed main tower, in 1597 and died the next year, leaving it to his son Hideyori. After Sekigahara in 1600 Tokugawa Ieyasu held power; he would besiege the castle in 1614–15.

image.file: File:The Siege of Osaka Castle.jpg
image.caption: Folding screen of the 1615 summer siege of Osaka Castle, painted in the 17th century for Kuroda Nagamasa.

kyoto.blurb: Home of the imperial court, Kyoto had been remade by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who added north–south streets, gathered temples along Teramachi and ringed the city with earthen odoi walls. In 1601 Tokugawa Ieyasu ordered Nijō Castle built here.

image.file: File:Rakuchu rakugai zu byobu (Fukuoka City Museum).jpg
image.caption: Scenes in and around the Capital, a pair of folding screens of Kyoto attributed to Kano Takanobu, Momoyama period (1568–1600).

istanbul.blurb: Constantinople was absorbing the Treaty of Karlowitz of 1699, which ceded large territories to the Habsburgs and Venice. Anger at Sultan Mustafa II's absence in Edirne would fuel the 1703 revolt that deposed him.

image.file: File:Procession through the Hippodrome, Constantinople (Aubry de La Mottraye's "Travels throughout Europe, Asia and into Part of Africa...," London, 1724, vol. I, plate 15) MET DP824505.jpg
image.caption: A procession through the Hippodrome of Constantinople, a print from Aubry de La Mottraye's Travels, published 1723–24.

tokyo.blurb: Rebuilt after the Great Fire of Meireki in 1657 with firebreaks and wider streets, the shogun's city had spread east of the Sumida River. It was the prosperous Genroku era, when the arts and architecture flourished.

image.file: File:Hishikawa Moronobu, Autumn at Asakusa; Viewing Cherry blossoms at Ueno Park, Edo period, Freer Gallery of Art.jpg
image.caption: Autumn at Asakusa and cherry-blossom viewing at Ueno in Edo, a pair of Edo-period folding screens by Hishikawa Moronobu (Freer Gallery of Art).

beijing.blurb: Qing capital since 1644, Beijing quartered Manchu, Mongol and Han banner troops by the Inner City gates. Northwest of the walls the Kangxi Emperor had built the Changchun Garden in 1684, and would soon begin the Yuanmingyuan.

image.file: File:Kangxi-Verbotene-Stadt1.jpg
image.caption: Detail of the Kangxi Emperor's Southern Inspection Tour scroll (1690s), showing the court awaiting his return to the Forbidden City in 1689.

london.blurb: Rebuilt in brick and stone after the Great Fire of 1666, London held the first service in Wren's new St Paul's Cathedral in 1697. By 1700 it handled 80% of England's imports, re-exporting silk, sugar, tea and tobacco.

image.file: File:City of London Ogilby and Morgan's Map of 1677.jpg
image.caption: Ogilby and Morgan's map of the City of London as rebuilt after the Great Fire, published 1677 (reduced copy).

paris.blurb: Louis XIV had moved the court to Versailles in 1671, yet Paris kept growing: the old walls were demolished to make way for boulevards, and the Place Vendôme was laid out in 1698. Around 1700 London overtook it in size.

image.file: File:Nicolas de Fer, Huitieme plan de Paris divisé en ses vingts quartiers, 1705.jpg
image.caption: Nicolas de Fer's map of Paris divided into its twenty quarters, published in 1705.

beijing.blurb: In 1750 the Qianlong Emperor began a palace by the Western Lake for his mother's 60th birthday, the future Summer Palace. At the Yuanmingyuan, the Jesuit Giuseppe Castiglione was designing European-style palaces, begun in 1747.

image.file: File:Beautiful Scene of the Square Pot.jpg
image.caption: One of the Forty Scenes of the Yuanmingyuan, an album painted for the Qianlong Emperor by his court painters in 1744.

tokyo.blurb: Tokugawa Yoshimune's Kyōhō Reforms had reshaped fire-prone Edo: from 1720 townspeople manned 48 iroha fire brigades, and tiled roofs became compulsory. After Yoshimune's death in 1751 the fireproofing drive faltered.

image.file: File:Large Perspective Picture of Evening Cool by Ryogoku Bridge by Okumura Masanobu.JPG
image.caption: Evening Cool by Ryōgoku Bridge in Edo, a perspective woodblock print by Okumura Masanobu, about 1748.

london.blurb: In 1750 Westminster Bridge opened, the first rival to London Bridge as a Thames crossing, and the Bow Street Runners began as a professional police force. New West End districts such as Mayfair pushed the city beyond its old limits.

image.file: File:Canaletto - Westminster Bridge, with the Lord Mayor's Procession on the Thames - Google Art Project.jpg
image.caption: Canaletto's Westminster Bridge, with the Lord Mayor's Procession on the Thames, painted in 1747.

istanbul.blurb: Mahmud I, enthroned by the 1730 revolt that ended the Tulip Period, was building the Nuruosmaniye Mosque by the Grand Bazaar: the first sultan's mosque in over a century and the first in the new Ottoman Baroque style.

image.file: File:Nuruosmaniye Camii.jpg
image.caption: The Nuruosmaniye Mosque, built 1748–1755, photographed in 2018.

paris.blurb: Paris was the hub of the Enlightenment: Diderot and d'Alembert's Encyclopédie began appearing in 1751, and writers met in cafés such as the Procope. Yet Voltaire complained in 1749 that the city centre was dark, cramped and hideous.

image.file: File:Turgot map of Paris, general map - Norman B. Leventhal Map Center.jpg
image.caption: Overview sheet of the Turgot map of Paris, published in 1739 and showing the city as surveyed in 1734–1736.

beijing.blurb: The Jiaqing Emperor ruled alone after his father Qianlong died in 1799. Beijing had turned away Britain's Macartney embassy, and Anhui opera troupes invited to court in 1790 were starting the blend that became Peking Opera.

image.file: File:徐扬京师生春诗意图轴.png
image.caption: Xu Yang's painting of Beijing in spring, Poetic Spring in the Capital, dated 1767.

london.blurb: On 12 July 1800 Prime Minister William Pitt helped lay the foundation stone of the West India Docks, London's first commercial wet docks, walled against the theft and delays that plagued the riverside wharves.

image.file: File:The West India Docks, as they appeared in March 1802 RMG PU1443.jpg
image.caption: The newly completed West India Docks as they appeared in March 1802, a print from the Gentleman's Magazine, October 1802.

guangzhou.blurb: Since 1757 Canton had been the sole legal port for most Western trade with China. European and American traders lived in the Thirteen Factories on the Pearl River, dealing only through the licensed Cohong merchants.

image.file: File:William Daniell - The European Factories at Canton in China - B1978.43.219 - Yale Center for British Art.jpg
image.caption: William Daniell's painting of the European factories on the waterfront at Canton, 1805.

tokyo.blurb: Edo was emerging from the Kansei Reforms of 1787–93, launched after famine and the Edo riots of 1787. Matsudaira Sadanobu cut city spending, stockpiled rice and in 1790 enforced Neo-Confucian orthodoxy, banning certain publications.

image.file: File:Famous-Places-of-Edo-1803-Kuwagata-Shoshin.jpg
image.caption: Famous Places of Edo (Edo meisho no e), a pictorial view of the city by Kuwagata Shoshin, first edition 1803.

istanbul.blurb: In 1800 Sultan Selim III built wooden barracks at Üsküdar, on the Asian shore, for the soldiers of his Nizam-ı Cedid, or New Order army. Rebel Janissaries opposed to his reforms burned them in 1806.

image.file: File:Vue général de Constantinople, prise du chemin de Buyuk Déré - Melling Antoine Ignace - 1819.jpg
image.caption: General view of Constantinople from the road to Büyükdere, an engraving after Antoine Ignace Melling, published in 1819.
